topicName: ACID Transactions on Object Storage (Time Travel, Vacuuming)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"ACID Transactions on Object Storage (Time Travel, Vacuuming)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional data warehousing relied on expensive storage SANs to provide ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) guarantees. Modern lakehouse architectures bring these guarantees directly to cost-effective cloud object storage (like AWS S3 or Azure Blob) using open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"How ACID Works on Object Storage"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Object storage is inherently immutable; you cannot update a file in place, you can only overwrite or delete it. Open table formats solve this by maintaining a transaction log (manifest files) that point to a collection of immutable data files (Parquet or ORC). A write operation adds new data files and commits a new transaction log atomically."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Atomicity: Transactions either completely succeed by writing a new log entry or fail without altering the current snapshot."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Consistency: Metadata validation checks prevent conflicting concurrent writes using Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Isolation: Readers query the snapshot state defined by the log version at the start of their query, unaffected by concurrent writes."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Durability: Backed by the high availability guarantees of cloud object storage providers."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Time Travel Capabilities"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because historical transaction logs and their corresponding data files are retained, users can query past states of the database. This is vital for auditing, reproducible machine learning, and rolling back accidental data corruption."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM sales_data FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP '2023-10-01 10:00:00';"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Vacuuming and Garbage Collection"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Over time, updates, deletes, and appends create orphaned data files and old log versions that are no longer referenced by active snapshots. The vacuum process (or garbage collection) permanently deletes these unreferenced files from object storage to reclaim storage costs."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"CALL system.expire_snapshots('catalog.db.sales_data', TIMESTAMP '2023-10-01 00:00:00');\nCALL system.remove_orphan_files('catalog.db.sales_data');"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Caution must be exercised when setting retention thresholds for vacuuming. Setting the retention window too short will break active time travel queries or long-running jobs currently reading older snapshots."}]
